### Q1. Random Walk with Momentum

```{r}
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(DBI)
aux <- read_xpt("data/AUX_I.XPT")
demo <- read_xpt("data/DEMO_I.XPT")
nhanes <- merge(
  aux,
  demo,
  by = "SEQN",
  all = FALSE
)

dim(nhanes)
```

After reviewing the official NHANES codebook, I found that the numeric missing-value codes are 7 and 9 for DMDCITZN, and 77 and 99 for INDHHIN2; RIAGENDR and DMDHHSZA have no numeric missing-value codes.

```{r}
nhanes$DMDCITZN[nhanes$DMDCITZN %in% c(7, 9)] <- NA
nhanes$INDHHIN2[nhanes$INDHHIN2 %in% c(77, 99)] <- NA

```

```{r}
r1 <- glm(
  AUXTWIDR ~ factor(RIAGENDR), family = poisson(), data = nhanes
)

r2 <- glm(AUXTWIDR ~ factor(RIAGENDR) + factor(DMDCITZN) + factor(DMDHHSZA) + factor(INDHHIN2),
  family = poisson(),
  data = nhanes
)

l1 <- glm(AUXTWIDL ~ factor(RIAGENDR), family = poisson(), data = nhanes
)

l2 <- glm(AUXTWIDL ~ factor(RIAGENDR) + factor(DMDCITZN) + factor(DMDHHSZA) + factor(INDHHIN2),
  family = poisson(),
  data = nhanes
)
```

```{r}

pseudo_r2 <- function(model) {
  null_model <- update(model, . ~ 1)

  1 - as.numeric(logLik(model)) /
    as.numeric(logLik(null_model))
}#calculate r2 from poisson model
get_coef_table <- function(model, model_name) {
  
  sm <- summary(model)$coefficients
  
  data.frame(
    Model = model_name,
    Predictor = rownames(sm),
    IRR = exp(sm[, "Estimate"]),
    P_value = sm[, "Pr(>|z|)"],
    row.names = NULL
  )
}

coef_table <- rbind(
  get_coef_table(r1, "1R"),
  get_coef_table(r2, "2R"),
  get_coef_table(l1, "1L"),
  get_coef_table(l2, "2L")
)

# remove intercept if you do not want to report it
coef_table <- coef_table[
  coef_table$Predictor != "(Intercept)",
]

coef_table$IRR <- round(coef_table$IRR, 3)
coef_table$P_value <- signif(coef_table$P_value, 3)

knitr::kable(
  coef_table,
  caption = "table for coefficients",
  col.names = c(
    "Model",
    "Predictor",
    "IRR",
    "p-value"
  )
)
model_table <- data.frame(
  Model = c("1R", "2R", "1L", "2L"),
  
  Outcome = c(
    "Right ear",
    "Right ear",
    "Left ear",
    "Left ear"
  ),
  
  n = c(
    nobs(r1),
    nobs(r2),
    nobs(l1),
    nobs(l2)
  ),
  
  Pseudo_R2 = c(
    pseudo_r2(r1),
    pseudo_r2(r2),
    pseudo_r2(l1),
    pseudo_r2(l2)
  ),
  
  AIC = c(
    AIC(r1),
    AIC(r2),
    AIC(l1),
    AIC(l2)
  )
)

model_table$Pseudo_R2 <- round(model_table$Pseudo_R2, 4)
model_table$AIC <- round(model_table$AIC, 1)

knitr::kable(
  model_table,
  caption = "table for model statistics",
  col.names = c(
    "Model",
    "Outcome",
    "n",
    "Pseudo-R2",
    "AIC"
  )
)

```

```{r}
library(emmeans)

pred_gender <- emmeans(
  l2,
  ~ RIAGENDR,
  type = "response"
)

pred_gender
pairs(pred_gender)
```

The predicted left-ear tympanometric width was 83.6 for males and 85.0 for females. The difference was statistically significant (p = 4.80e-06 \< 0.05), indicating that females have a slightly higher predicted left-ear tympanometric width than males.

## Q2

```{r}
library(DBI)
library(RSQLite)
con <- dbConnect(
  SQLite(),
  "data/sakila_master.db"
) #get the data
dbListTables(con)
dbListFields(con, "customer")

```

### Q2A

```{r}
 
customer <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM customer;")

head(customer, 5)
 

result_r <- customer %>% group_by(store_id) %>%
  summarise(n_customer = n(), pct_active = mean(as.numeric(active)) * 100)

result_sql <- dbGetQuery(con,
  " SELECT store_id, COUNT(customer_id) AS n_customer, AVG(active) * 100 AS pct_active FROM customer GROUP BY store_id; "
)
result_r
result_sql

```

Then get the time benchmark

```{r}
library(microbenchmark)

microbenchmark(
  R = {
        customer <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM customer;")

        result_r <- customer %>% group_by(store_id) %>%
        summarise(n_customer = n(), pct_active = mean(as.numeric(active)) * 100)
  },

  SQL = {
    dbGetQuery(con,
       " SELECT store_id, COUNT(customer_id) AS n_customer, AVG(active) * 100 AS pct_active FROM customer GROUP BY store_id; "
      )
  },

  times = 100
)
```

The SQL approach is much faster, with an average runtime of about 805 ms compared with 3116 ms for the R approach. Overall, SQL is nearly four times faster.

### Q2B

```{r}
staff  <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT first_name, last_name, address_id FROM staff;")
address <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM address;")
city <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM city;")
country<- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM country;")
staff_sql <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT staff.first_name || ' ' || staff.last_name AS name, country.country FROM staff
INNER JOIN address
  ON staff.address_id = address.address_id
INNER JOIN city
  ON address.city_id = city.city_id
INNER JOIN country
  ON city.country_id = country.country_id;")
staff_sql
staff_r <- staff %>% inner_join(address, by = 'address_id') %>% inner_join(city, by = 'city_id') %>% inner_join(country, by = 'country_id') %>% mutate(name = paste(first_name, last_name)) %>% select(name, country)
staff_r
```

```{r}
microbenchmark(
SQL = { dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT staff.first_name || ' ' || staff.last_name AS name, country.country FROM staff
INNER JOIN address
  ON staff.address_id = address.address_id
INNER JOIN city
  ON address.city_id = city.city_id
INNER JOIN country
  ON city.country_id = country.country_id;")},
 
R = { 
  staff  <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT first_name, last_name, address_id FROM staff;")
address <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM address;")
city <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM city;")
country<- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM country;")
  staff %>% inner_join(address, by = 'address_id') %>% inner_join(city, by = 'city_id') %>% inner_join(country, by = 'country_id') %>% mutate(name = paste(first_name, last_name)) %>% select(name, country)},

  times = 100
)
```

The SQL approach is much faster, with an average runtime of about 309 ms compared with 5348 ms for the R approach.

### Q2C

```{r}

box_sql <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT DISTINCT film.title, payment.amount FROM film
INNER JOIN inventory
  ON film.film_id = inventory.film_id
INNER JOIN rental
  ON inventory.inventory_id = rental.inventory_id
INNER JOIN payment
  ON rental.rental_id = payment.rental_id WHERE payment.amount = (SELECT MAX(amount) FROM payment);")
box_sql
film <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM film;")
inventory <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM inventory;")
rental <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM rental;")
payment <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM payment;")
box_r <- film %>% inner_join(inventory, by = "film_id") %>% inner_join(rental, by = "inventory_id") %>% 
  inner_join(payment, by = "rental_id") %>% filter(amount == max(amount)) %>% select(title, amount) %>%
  distinct()
box_r
```

```{r}
microbenchmark(
SQL = { dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT DISTINCT film.title, payment.amount FROM film
INNER JOIN inventory
  ON film.film_id = inventory.film_id
INNER JOIN rental
  ON inventory.inventory_id = rental.inventory_id
INNER JOIN payment
  ON rental.rental_id = payment.rental_id WHERE payment.amount = (SELECT MAX(amount) FROM payment);")
},
R = {
film <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM film;")
inventory <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM inventory;")
rental <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM rental;")
payment <- dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT * FROM payment;")
box_r <- film %>% inner_join(inventory, by = "film_id") %>% inner_join(rental, by = "inventory_id") %>% 
  inner_join(payment, by = "rental_id") %>% filter(amount == max(amount)) %>% select(title, amount) %>%
  distinct()
}
)
```

The SQL approach is much faster, with an average runtime of about 1 ms compared with 37 ms for the R approach.

```{r}
aus <- read_csv("data/au-500.csv")

com_data <- aus %>%
  filter(endsWith(web, ".com"))
 
perc_com <- nrow(com_data) / nrow(aus) * 100
perc_com
```

There are no websites ending in `.com`, so the percentage is **0%**. In fact, all websites in `au-500.csv` end in `.com.au`.

```{r}
aus$emailDomain <- sub(".*@", "", aus$email)
count(aus, emailDomain,sort = TRUE)
```

The most common domain name is hotmail.com, which appears 114 times.

```{r}
aus$has_NAC <- grepl("[^A-Za-z0-9, ]", aus$company_name)
percent_NAC <- sum(aus$has_NAC) / nrow(aus)
percent_NAC
aus$has_NACnand <- grepl("[^A-Za-z0-9, &]", aus$company_name)
percent_NACnand <- sum(aus$has_NACnand) / nrow(aus)
percent_NACnand
```

8.4% of all company names contain a non-alphabetic character excluding commas and whitespace. 0.2 of all company names contain a non-alphabetic character excluding commas, '&' and whitespace.

```{r}

aus$phone1 <- paste0(
  substr(gsub("-", "", aus$phone1), 1, 4),
  "-",
  substr(gsub("-", "", aus$phone1), 5, 7),
  "-",
  substr(gsub("-", "", aus$phone1), 8, 10)
)

aus$phone2 <- paste0(
  substr(gsub("-", "", aus$phone2), 1, 4),
  "-",
  substr(gsub("-", "", aus$phone2), 5, 7),
  "-",
  substr(gsub("-", "", aus$phone2), 8, 10)
)
head(aus, 10)
```

```{r}
#if not end with numbers, use 0
aus$apt_num <- as.numeric(
  ifelse(
    is.na(str_extract(aus$address, "\\d+$")),
    "0",
    str_extract(aus$address, "\\d+$")
  )
)
hist(log(aus$apt_num), main = 'A histogram of the log of the apartment numbers for all addresses', xlab = 'log of the apartment numbers')
```

```{r}
apt <- aus$apt_num[aus$apt_num > 0]
first_digit <- as.numeric(substr(as.character(apt), 1, 1))
observed_prob <- table(first_digit) / sum(table(first_digit))
observed_prob

digits <- 1:9
benford_prob <- log10(1 + 1 / digits)
benford_prob
```

They don't appear to follow the Benford's law.

```{r}
chisq.test(
  observed_prob,
  p = benford_prob
)
```

Runnning a chi-square test, the p value is far larger than 0.05, so we reject the null hypothesis that the apartment number follows the Benford's law. The apartment numbers would not pass as real data.
